help.title: Help
help.intro: LogCarve shows deterministic analytics over one configured access-log source. This page explains the filters, labels and limits you will meet on every data view.
help.filters_body: Every data view shares one filter bar: site, source, time range, display timezone, traffic and bot selectors, method, status and text search. Applying a new window always restarts at the first result page; switching pages keeps the full filter set. A traffic quick view replaces the traffic, bot, category, provider and purpose selectors together, a status quick view replaces status and status class together, and Largest responses only presets the Requests sort; each keeps the site, source, window and all other matchers and resets paging. Contradictory combinations are rejected instead of silently widened.
help.offsets_body: Requests are stored and filtered in UTC. The timezone selector only changes the display. Each zone option shows its signed UTC offset for the applied window start; daylight saving may shift offsets inside longer windows. Links and exports always carry full UTC instants.
help.labels_body: Bot names come from a versioned claim catalog; the dropdown shows plain names while rule IDs, versions and meanings stay exact in the API and detail panels. Categories read as AI crawlers, Search crawlers, SEO tools or Automation tools, and an empty provider or purpose reads as Unspecified. Browser-like rows are potential user traffic only: access logs alone cannot prove people, sessions, indexing, training use or conversions.
help.identity_body: Bot names are identified from User-Agent; identity not verified. True verification needs the original client address plus reverse and forward DNS checks (or approved published range matching), and original addresses are intentionally discarded, so LogCarve never proves a bot is fake or genuine. See the optional Google verification reference for what real verification requires; it is documentation only and LogCarve performs no automatic network checks.
help.privacy_body: Client addresses are HMAC-pseudonymized and original IPs never leave the import host. Query values are discarded, Referer data is minimized and secrets in paths are masked. Raw log lines and original IPs never appear in exports, error messages, API responses or assistant evidence. No GeoIP or country claims are made.
help.explorer_body: The Requests explorer lists sanitized rows in any allowlisted server sort (newest/oldest time, client, method, path, status, bytes ascending/descending) with stable timestamp/id tie-breaks and server pagination. Each row expands to a details panel with the 200-character User-Agent sample, referrer host, traffic and bot metadata, full client pseudonym, UTC and shown timestamps with offset, rule reference and the unavailable-timing note. Choosing a sort restarts at the first page; paging links advance through pages while keeping the sort direction and the full filter scope.
help.conflict_body: A conflicting-bot-identity candidate means one User-Agent carries unambiguous named bot tokens for two or more distinct providers (for example Googlebot and bingbot in one string). The known set is limited to Googlebot plus Googlebot-Image, Googlebot-News and Googlebot-Video (all Google), bingbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, AhrefsBot, SemrushBot, MJ12bot, YandexBot and Baiduspider; underscore or hyphen affixes such as some_Googlebot_clone or my-Googlebot-tool are not counted as identity. This is a potential spoof or inconsistency lead only: identity is not verified, nothing is removed from counts, and no automatic blocking follows. True verification needs the original client address plus reverse and forward DNS checks, and original addresses are intentionally discarded, so LogCarve never proves a bot fake or genuine. The absence of this candidate also proves nothing; unknown agents stay labelled unknown or unverified.
help.troubleshooting_body: No rows usually means the selected window has no matching events: widen the range, clear the search, or check the Data Sources page for failed or partial imports. A rejected filter shows which value was invalid; nothing is silently widened. If the assistant is disabled or over budget, every deterministic table keeps working.
help.api_body: Browser pages need an admin session login. Programmatic access uses scoped API tokens with the analytics:read scope instead; tokens cannot open browser pages, import data or reach the assistant. Responses are paginated, scoped to site and time, stamped in UTC and contract-versioned.

requests.client_sort_note: Client sorts by stable pseudonym, never by original address.
error.csrf_required: The request was rejected (session check failed). Reload the page and retry.
error.auth_required: An admin session is required. Log in and retry.
privacy.ip_body: Originals are decrypted only for the local admin Requests view, masked before rendering, and never reach the API, exports, errors or assistant tools. Display masking is not anonymity.
privacy.ip_mode_full_hint: Default when no preference is stored.
privacy.ip_key_missing: No decryption key configured: originals show as unavailable.
privacy.ip_corrupt: Stored display preferences were invalid and were safely ignored: showing pseudonyms only. Save valid settings to change the view.
privacy.ip_unavailable_no_key: Original unavailable: no decryption key is configured. Reprocess the read-only source after configuring a key; analytics are unaffected.
privacy.ip_unavailable_invalid_key: Original unavailable: the configured key is invalid. Check the server key; analytics are unaffected.
privacy.ip_unavailable_decrypt_failed: Original unavailable: decryption failed (wrong key or tampered data). Reprocess the read-only source with the correct key.
privacy.ip_unavailable_not_stored: Original unavailable: this record predates encrypted storage or was never enriched. Reprocess the read-only source to enrich it; pseudonyms and counts are unchanged.
privacy.ip_unavailable_scoped: Original unavailable: scoped IPv6 forms are not displayed. Pseudonyms and counts are unchanged.
privacy.ip_pseudonym_only: Pseudonyms only: originals stay encrypted. Counts and filters are unchanged.
privacy.ip_mask_note: Masked suffixes are removed before rendering and are absent from the page.
privacy.ip_search_hint: Enter one exact IPv4 or IPv6 address in its stored spelling. Equivalent spellings (compressed vs expanded) are distinct records. The address is translated to its pseudonym and never appears in the address bar.
privacy.ip_search_invalid: Enter a single valid IPv4 or IPv6 address.
privacy.export_note: Downloads contain stable pseudonyms only, never original addresses, regardless of the display mode.

perf.other_rows: Other: {count} further requests outside the shown top values

ref.title: Referrers
ref.no_targets: No broken inbound links in this window.
ref.match_note: Lowercase hostname equality; ports, userinfo and query values are never stored; only http/https referrers are kept.
ref.all_note: Every stored referrer counts, whatever the response status; missing scheme or path reads as Unknown and never implies direct traffic.
ref.no_sources: No referring pages in this window.
ref.related_broken_title: Related host and target requests with status 404; different source paths on the same host are included.
ref.related_all_title: Related requests carrying this referring host; different source paths on the same host are included.
journeys.title: Request journeys
journeys.list_note: Technical groupings of stored requests by client pseudonym and sanitized User-Agent with a 30-minute inactivity split. Never visitors, people, browser sessions or clicks.
journeys.no_groups: No request journeys in this window for the selected filters.
journeys.min_requests_note: Only journeys with at least this many shown requests are listed; totals stay exact.
journeys.detail_note: Bounded chronological sample of stored requests for one opaque journey ID. Filters cannot move journey boundaries; the entry is the base-scope first request.
journeys.no_detail: Select a journey to inspect its bounded chronological timeline.
journeys.detail_not_found: No journey matches that opaque ID in this window and filter scope.
journeys.entries_note: Each entry is the journey base-scope first request, so filters cannot move entries. Complete and window-edge partial journeys are counted together with both shares shown; partial means the journey may start or end outside the window.
journeys.no_entries: No entry paths in this window for the selected filters.
journeys.timeline_truncated: Showing the first {shown} of {total} timeline rows.
journeys.gap_note: A new journey starts only when the gap to the previous event of the same client and agent strictly exceeds 30 minutes; exactly 30 minutes continues the journey.
security.rate_note: Average spreads every matching row over the full validated window; the peak counts only the busiest whole UTC minute over the same rule scope.
security.challenge_note: Status 401 is an authentication challenge, never evidence of a failed login by a person.
